subject: Potential service-account key exposure — IRP, SIG/CAIQ evidence request and follow-up
messages:
From: OpsSec Team <opssec@finservco.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Audra Kline <audra.k@finservco.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential service-account key exposure - urgent info request

Diego —

We detected activity originating from one of your service-account keys that appears to have been staged in a public S3 object (bucket: fsci-prod-backups). This started at ~2027-06-13T22:40UTC and continued for a short window. Our security stack flagged credentials used from an unfamiliar IP and exfiltration of a small number of metadata files.

We need to understand the exposure vector and timeline. Specifically, can you provide:
- Your Incident Response Plan (IRP) and the primary escalation contact for IR events
- Any SIG/CAIQ answers you can share relevant to key management and rotation controls
- Forensics artifacts (auth logs, key rotation audit) for the 2027-06-13 to 2027-06-14 window

This is time-sensitive for our compliance team and auditors. Please reply with an initial ack and ETA for evidence delivery.

Thanks,
OpsSec Team
FinServCo
[Attachment: detection-alert-20270614.json (JSON, 28KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: OpsSec Team <opssec@finservco.com>
Cc: Audra Kline <audra.k@finservco.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential service-account key exposure - urgent info request

Acknowledged — thanks for the heads up, OpsSec.

Sofia and Markus: can you triage immediately and assemble the artifacts requested? Priorities:
1) Confirm whether the key was compromised or accidentally committed; rotate and revoke if confirmed.
2) Pull auth logs, key rotation audit, and any S3 access logs for the 2027-06-13 20:00UTC -> 2027-06-14 00:00UTC window.
3) Prepare a short IRP extract that shows our notification and escalation steps (we'll redact unrelated internal contact info).

OpsSec / Audra: quick questions to narrow scope — do you have the exact object path or any identifiers from the alert? Any IOCs (IPs, hashes) would speed triage.

I'll own the communication. ETA for an initial artifact bundle: 6 hours, with an interim status in 90 minutes.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential service-account key exposure - triage update (internal)

Diego / Markus —

Quick triage update:
- We located the service account (sa-ingest-2026) and confirmed a key was present in an old backup object (s3://redwood-archives/2022/ingest/sa-key.bak). Looks like an accidental inclusion from a legacy backup job.
- Key was rotated and previous key marked revoked at 2027-06-14T08:45:12-07:00. We have disabled the backup job and queued a full scan of archive buckets.
- Captured relevant auth logs (token usage, IPs) and S3 access logs. Preliminary indicator: access from 34.89.12.110 at 2027-06-13T22:47UTC.

Artifacts we will bundle: forensics-logs-2027-06-14.tar.gz (auth + s3 logs), rpm_key_rotation_audit.csv (rotation events), and an interim IRP extract (redwood_irp_v3.2.pdf) that shows steps taken.

We will redact internal-only notes and reduce PII; will follow the redaction checklist in SOC2 evidence handling guidelines.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, OpsSec Team <opssec@finservco.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: IRP extract and SIG/CAIQ workbook (interim)

Diego / Sofia / OpsSec —

Attached is an interim packet:
- redwood_irp_v3.2.pdf — redacted IRP extract (pages 3-8 cover evidence collection, escalation timeline)
- sig-caiq-answers-partial-2027-06.xlsx — SIG/CAIQ workbook with answered items around key management, rotation, and secrets handling (marked PARTIAL where we need legal review)
- rpm_key_rotation_audit.csv — rotation audit for sa-ingest-2026 (shows previous rotation events and the revoke action taken at 2027-06-14T08:45:12-07:00)

I uploaded the full forensics bundle to the shared drive (link below). I recommend we send the IRP extract + workbook + a link to the forensics bundle rather than attaching the entire tar file via email.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4-redwood-incident-evidence

If OpsSec prefers a signed NDA scan or additional redaction before transfer, let me know — otherwise I'll hand this off for external delivery.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood_irp_v3.2.pdf (PDF, 420KB); sig-caiq-answers-partial-2027-06.xlsx (Excel, 210KB); rpm_key_rotation_audit.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: OpsSec Team <opssec@finservco.com>, Audra Kline <audra.k@finservco.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential service-account key exposure - IRP, SIG/CAIQ evidence request and follow-up

Audra / OpsSec —

Thank you for flagging this. Summary and artifacts below: 

Incident summary (short):
- Timeline: possible exposure window 2027-06-13T22:40UTC -> 2027-06-13T22:50UTC.
- Root cause: legacy backup object contained an older service-account key for sa-ingest-2026. This appears to be accidental; not the result of lateral compromise.
- Mitigation: key rotated and previous key revoked at 2027-06-14T08:45:12-07:00, backup job disabled, archive scan in progress.

Delivered artifacts (links/attachments):
- Redacted IRP extract: redwood_irp_v3.2.pdf (attached) — includes our notification and escalation matrix and evidence handling steps.
- SIG/CAIQ workbook (partial): sig-caiq-answers-partial-2027-06.xlsx (attached) — answers relevant to secrets management; we note a few items flagged for legal review.
- Forensics bundle (drive link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4-redwood-incident-evidence — contains forensics-logs-2027-06-14.tar.gz (auth + S3 access logs) and rpm_key_rotation_audit.csv. We will not send the full tar over email for size and access control reasons.

Next steps we propose:
1) OpsSec review the artifacts and confirm whether you need a full signed attestation or additional redactions.
2) If you need a more formal postmortem doc suitable for auditors, we can produce a controlled version with a cover letter and an executive timeline (ETA 3 business days).

If you need anything earlier than that, reply to this thread and I will prioritize.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
